paths.path: ~/.config/hatari/hatari.cfg (legacy ~/.hatari/ is used instead while it exists; /etc/hatari.cfg is read first; -c/--configfile adds overrides)
paths.naming: Controller syntax is INI `[Joystick0]`/`[Joystick1]`: `nJoystickMode`, SDL device `nJoyId`, fire-button indices `nJoyBut1/2/3Index`; directions use SDL axes 0/1 or hat 0

paths.path: In place inside the mounted writable floppy (.ST/.MSA/.DIM) or hard-disk/GEMDOS images; Hatari writes no per-game sidecar save files, and ZIP/gz-packed disk images are never written back (writes go through only when the image is not write-protected, see --wp-floppyA on/off/auto)
paths.naming: Saves keep the mounted disk image's own name (game.st/.msa/.dim); there are no separate .sav files per floppy/hd image
evidence: docs:manual "Hatari does not save disk images back to *.ZIP files so your highscores and savegames are lost if you load the game from such a zipped disk image"

paths.path: Whole-machine memory snapshots; default file is <Hatari home>/hatari.sav with auto.sav for the auto-snapshot, renamed freely via the Memory dialog (AltGr+k save / AltGr+l load)
paths.naming: A single configured snapshot file (szMemoryCaptureFileName, default hatari.sav) plus auto.sav; any filename can be chosen in the save file selector; snapshots are not interchangeable between Hatari versions
evidence: docs:manual The Memory Dialog save/restore snapshot

paths.path: TOS ROM image, by default <prefix>/share/hatari/tos.img, or any file passed via --tos / set in the [ROM] szTosImageFileName setting; EmuTOS is shipped with official releases as the free alternative
paths.naming: TOS ROM convention is tos.img; --tos or [ROM] szTosImageFileName may select another filename, including an EmuTOS image; no canonical checksum is declared
evidence: docs:manual Installation of a TOS ROM (rename to tos.img or use --tos)

linux.notes: The Hatari home resolves from $HOME (not XDG variables), so Lunchbox's private HOME plus -c isolates reads and writes while native saves stay in the session directory.

paths.path: ~/.var/app/org.tuxfamily.hatari/.config/hatari/hatari.cfg (flatpak gives the app its own $HOME, so the same HOME-relative .config/hatari layout lands under ~/.var/app)
paths.naming: Same INI `[Joystick0]`/`[Joystick1]` syntax as native: `nJoyId`, `nJoyBut1/2/3Index`, and SDL axis 0/1 or hat 0 directions

paths.path: Same as native Linux: writes land inside the mounted writable disk images inside the sandbox-visible filesystem
paths.naming: Saves keep the mounted disk image's own name; no sidecar save files
Single configured memory-snapshot file, default hatari.sav plus auto.sav; filenames freely selectable via the GUI

paths.path: TOS image inside the sandbox (user-selected via --tos/[ROM] szTosImageFileName, e.g. tos.img or the bundled EmuTOS)
paths.naming: TOS ROM convention is tos.img; --tos or [ROM] szTosImageFileName may select another filename, including EmuTOS; no canonical checksum is declared
evidence: docs:manual Installation of a TOS ROM

linux-flatpak.notes: Flathub build exists (org.tuxfamily.hatari); Lunchbox's native Hatari integration requires native Linux, not Flatpak.

paths.path: <home>\AppData\Local\Hatari\hatari.cfg (home from HOMEDRIVE+HOMEPATH; legacy ~/.hatari and the global hatari.cfg are read with the same precedence)
paths.naming: Same INI `[Joystick0]`/`[Joystick1]` syntax as native: `nJoyId`, `nJoyBut1/2/3Index`, and SDL axis 0/1 or hat 0 directions
evidence: source:src/paths.c WIN32 HATARI_HOME_DIR "AppData\\Local\\Hatari" and HOMEDRIVE/HOMEPATH home resolution
